one_liner: Navy contracting officer who buys supplies and services for military family and morale programs in the DC region and supervises a small procurement team.
fit_summary: This job requires a year of hands-on contracting at NF-03 or GS-11/12 level (soliciting, negotiating, awarding and administering contracts, price and cost analysis, FAR and NAF rules) plus supervision. Daniel's proposal and purchasing work at IEM was on the contractor side, and his supervision is a five-person intake team in 2019, so skip it.
eligibility: Open to the public (NAF position), so no federal status or veterans' preference is needed.
One full year of specialized contracting experience equivalent to NF-03 or GS-11/12, in federal service or the commercial contracting sector.
Education: a bachelor's degree in any field, or 24 semester hours in business-related fields. His M.A. (George Mason, 2016) implies a bachelor's.
Security clearance is listed as 'Other'; expect a background investigation for a Navy installation role.
Must be able to act as an appointed Contracting Officer within warrant limits; supervisory duties make up 25% of the role.
strategy: Skip this one: his IEM proposal writing and medical-supply purchasing were contractor-side and rarely count as a year of NF-03 or GS-11 contracting, and his supervision is limited to a five-person intake team.

More realistic targets are entry-level GS-7/9 Contract Specialist (1102) roles open to the public, or FEMA and Virginia emergency management and legislative affairs posts, which build on his IEM and policy background.
resume_bullets: As part of the logistics team, procured medical supplies, equipment and vaccines for COVID-19 sites in six states and set up vendor relationships (2021–2022).
Led proposal writing in answer to government solicitations (2019–2024).
interview_questions: Walk us through how you determined a price was fair and reasonable on a recent procurement.
How would you handle a purchase card request that looks like construction rather than supplies or services?
Describe a time you advised a program manager who wanted a procurement approach that conflicted with regulations.
How would you prioritize work and develop a small team of contract specialists and procurement technicians?
watch_outs: His resume lacks the required year of hands-on contracting at the NF-03 or GS-11/12 level, so an ineligible rating is likely.
Patuxent River, MD is a long commute from Manassas. Telework is eligible, but the job is not remote.
NAF pay bands are separate from GS, and there is no promotion potential beyond this role.
